resolution: User riffed on building a surf map at the --massive scale. Assessed feasibility against the codebase (no code change, analysis + offer): the bones already exist — ramps render via INSTANCE_SHAPE_RAMP (worldGeometry.ts pushRamp) and the no-V8 loader collides them as walkable-slope heightfields (registerRampHeightfield, RAMP_WALKABLE_SLOPE_COS), and spatial windowing already handles ramp heightfields, so a kilometers-long surf ribbon is just more static instances = effectively free to render at 240fps (a scale Source BSP surf maps physically cannot reach). What's missing is the surf MOVEMENT: framework/game/movement.zig only has integrateHorizontal (ground accel + friction). Surf needs (1) slide-along-plane on steep faces — project gravity down the ramp normal with near-zero friction instead of treating >~53deg as a wall, using the heightfield surface normal already available; and (2) Source-style air-strafe — capped air acceleration perpendicular to view while airborne, wired into game_physics.step when off-ground. Offered to build a surf movement mode + a procedural --surf ribbon generator (game play --surf), starting with the movement feel on a short test ramp then scaling to a ribbon. Awaiting the user's go-ahead.
